episode_title: Ensemble Capital Second Quarter 2024 Portfolio Update

real_qa.q: Why did the S&P 500 return 15.3% in the first half of 2024 while the average stock in the index returned only 5%?
real_qa.r: The S&P 500's outperformance was driven by massive concentration in a handful of mega-cap stocks, particularly NVIDIA, which was up 345% over the five-quarter period. The Magnificent Seven stocks—Tesla, Amazon, Apple, Google, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Facebook—returned 94.9% as a group, while the average stock returned only 16.2%. This concentration is historically unprecedented outside the dot-com bubble, with the five largest companies now making up a quarter of the entire index.

real_qa.q: How does NVIDIA's 345% five-quarter return compare to other Magnificent Seven stocks?
real_qa.r: NVIDIA is up a shocking 345% over the past five quarters, rising to become the most valuable company in the world. In comparison, Microsoft is only up 57%, Apple is up 29%, Tesla is down 5%, while Facebook has outperformed significantly. The Magnificent Seven as a group returned 94.9%, but NVIDIA alone is the primary driver of this outperformance.

real_qa.q: What valuation multiples do mega-cap stocks trade at compared to the S&P 500 average?
real_qa.r: NVIDIA trades at a P/E of 70, Amazon at 54, Microsoft at 40 times, Apple at 34 times, and Tesla at 100 times despite being down more than half from its all-time high. The market cap weighted S&P 500 has seen its P/E ratio soar to 25 times, essentially the highest valuation ever afforded the S&P 500 outside of recessions or the dot-com bubble, while the average stock's P/E ratio trends at a reasonable 17 to 18 times.

real_qa.q: What percentage of S&P 500 stocks have outperformed the broader index in 2024?
real_qa.r: Only 25% of stocks in the S&P 500 have outperformed the broader index so far this year. Last year, less than 30% of stocks outperformed. This represents the most dramatic deviation of at least the last half century, with fewer stocks beating the market today than even during the peak years of the dot-com bubble, when historically about 50% of stocks outperform and 50% underperform in a normal year.

real_qa.q: How much did Illumina's sequencing cost per human genome decline from 2010 to 2021?
real_qa.r: Illumina drove down the cost of sequencing an entire human genome from over $100,000 a decade ago down to just $600 with its NovaSeq 6000 high-end instrument, representing a 99% reduction in cost from 2010 to 2021. Despite this massive cost reduction, Illumina's revenue actually increased from $1 billion to $4.5 billion because applications and volumes of gene sequencing exploded higher, enabled by the greater affordability.

real_qa.q: What is the market size potential for Grail's multi-cancer early detection screening test?
real_qa.r: Grail's multi-cancer early detection screening (MCED) test could detect 50 different types of cancer from a single non-invasive blood drop across a market that could be as large as hundreds of millions of people globally. Currently, only standardized tests exist for five types of cancer—breast, prostate, colon, cervical, and lung—while about 8% of cancer deaths occur from cancers without recommended screening.
